## Findings by module

### directing-1

- **confirmed** (ch-001 director as conceptual artist): Niculescu describes the theatre director as a conceptual artist, an architect and a poet, whose job is to build live performances expressing ideas about life. Supports the module 1 framing of the director as an author of the whole production.
- **extended** (ch-001 director as necessity and messiah): The article's history: realists found the director necessary, and the rebels (Appia, Craig, Meyerhold, Copeau, Piscator, Brecht) cast him as the messiah of a new theatrical synthesis. Usable as a short history of the role, labelled as this article's account.
- **note** (ch-001 Stanislavski quotation): The article quotes Stanislavski: there is no stage director who can produce a piece without first finding the directing idea. The quote is taken from Cole and Chinoy (1963), a secondary source. Check the wording against Stanislavski before quoting it.
- **note** (ch-001 history dates): The article dates Leone de Sommi's treatise on stage direction to 1550. It is usually dated 1556. Check the date before any lesson uses it.

### directing-6

- **extended** (ch-001 giving objects a theatrical identity): Niculescu argues that puppets, masks and animated objects must get a theatrical identity and a dramaturgical function, and that the director must explore the dramatic potential of each object in its relation to space. Relevant to module 6 on space and designers.
